### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **53** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 39 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cdf0aef0e4aed0d150d9ad0a5e8cf6ff5f2c6f95` — the merge of head `efaf66a5138a35245ce0dc2ccb7b5eea0e02d794` into base `5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cdf0aef0e4aed0d150d9ad0a5e8cf6ff5f2c6f95 && git checkout cdf0aef0e4aed0d150d9ad0a5e8cf6ff5f2c6f95
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31 efaf66a5138a35245ce0dc2ccb7b5eea0e02d794 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31 && git merge --no-ff efaf66a5138a35245ce0dc2ccb7b5eea0e02d794

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5a871e4e41b110d5d4b0cdcc325a75723740bb31` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The 23 declarations — RIGHT on the set, RIGHT on 22 operations, and `sys_user`'s `select` is the seat's accepted exception.** The declarers are exactly ruling E′ item 3's list: the seven `sys_scim_*` projections, `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks`, the thirteen of the `_self` / `_org_members` list, and `sys_audit_log` (in `plugin-audit`, which owns the ledger under ADR-0029 K2). Each of the 22 non-merged declarations is `member_default`'s literal for the object with `object` dropped, read against `default-permission-sets.ts` at this head: `select` with `user_id == current_user.id` on the four SCIM `_self` tables, `sys_account`, `sys_team_member`, `sys_oauth_access_token` and `sys_oauth_refresh_token`; `select` with `id == null` on `sys_scim_group`, `sys_scim_group_member`, `sys_scim_connection_binding`, `sys_verification` and `sys_jwks`; `all` with `user_id == current_user.id` on `sys_session`, `sys_two_factor`, `sys_user_preference`, `sys_api_key`, `sys_device_code`, `sys_oauth_consent` and `sys_oauth_application`; `all` with `id == current_user.organization_id` on `sys_organization`; `select` with `tenant_id == current_user.organization_id` on `sys_audit_log`. `organization_admin` carries the same literal for each, and `viewer_readonly` the same predicate under `select` (pinned per object). No identity object is missing and no platform-global object declares one: the pin enumerates every object `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `AuditPlugin` register and asserts the declarer set equals the 23 and that `sys_metadata`, `sys_job`, `sys_migration` and `sys_platform_setting` carry none (`sys_presence` and `sys_flow_dispatch` live outside its import set, as the first report said; the tree-wide grep of `defaultRowScope` finds no declarer outside the 23 and the fixtures). `sys_user` is `select` with `id == current_user.id || id in current_user.org_user_ids`, where `member_default` spells `sys_user_self` as `all`; the release 6259391225 accepted `select` on the dev's reasoning (the peer arm must not reach a write). One reading to put on record: for a no-baseline principal granted a write on `sys_user`, the `select`-only default does reach the write by derivation (`computeLayeredRlsFilter` at `:7369` re-collects `select` when the write class carries no `using`), so its derived update scope is `self || peers` — the same rows an `all` declaration would admit, narrower than the unbounded write it had before, and never wider than before. A baseline holder keeps `member_default`'s `sys_user_self(all)` on writes. Not a defect; a fact #24484 must keep (see ③).

**2. `sys_user`'s ONE `||` policy — RIGHT for every producer that reaches it, and the edge is fail-closed.**
- *Union of the two literals.* `RLSCompiler.compileFilter` lowers the merged predicate to `$or` of the two arms whenever `current_user.org_user_ids` is an array (`[]` included), so the admitted rows are exactly the union the two literals OR-combine to; with the variable unresolved the whole policy is refused and the compiled Layer 1 is the deny filter, so the admitted set is `[]` where the two literals apart admit `[u_me]`. Both are pinned (the branch's unit pin on three contexts and the unresolved case) and the three producers are pinned on the real stack in `service-automation`: request (`resolveAuthzContextInScope` copies `grants.org_user_ids`, seeded `[userId]` and widened to the organisation's `sys_member` rows under a tenant, `[]` for the anonymous envelope), `runAs: 'user'` flow (`resolveRunContext` asks the grants bridge whenever the context carries no list, `plugin.ts` returns the resolver's list), and `runAs: 'user'` hook from a hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId }` (`ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]`, one `resolveUserAuthzGrants` call, `needsPeers` on `!Array.isArray`). In each the captured context carries an array and the served rows equal the literals' union on that same context. Right.
- *Other readers of `sys_user` with no list.* The MCP agent: `assembleExecutionContext` copies `authz.org_user_ids` onto the agent envelope and keeps `userId` as the human (`:316`–`:339`), and `resolveDelegatorContext` hands the live principal's list to the delegator leg, so both legs resolve the peer arm. The stdio MCP door resolves through the same `resolveAuthzContext`. SCIM: no package reads `sys_user` in a user context on a SCIM path (the only `sys_scim_user` readers outside platform-objects and plugin-security are `cli`'s ownership inventory and `service-settings`, system paths). The sharing plugin's `{ ...authz, isSystem: false }` and explain's `buildContextForUser` both come from the core resolver. A flow run suspended before #24495 resumes without run setup (`resume` at `:7212` never calls `resolveRunContext`; only `execute` at `:6654` and the entry at `:13233` do), so it carries no list until it ends: the dev's class is right. No other `isSystem: false` producer exists in non-test source (`assemble-execution-context.ts:337`, `engine.ts:21836`, `sharing-plugin.ts:1011`, `runtime-identity.ts:267`; `principal-session-mint-test-support.ts` is test support). No escalation is owed.
- *The resolver-failure edge.* `installRunAsApi`'s rejection arm installs the unseeded pin and warns once; `resolveRunContext`'s catch keeps the trigger's identity and warns. Under the merged predicate such a read admits `[]`, own row included; nothing is widened. Fail-closed, as records 6265937412 ① and 6263414965 ③ accepted; `sys-user.object.ts`'s comment states it. Right.

**3. ③.11 on the real declarations — RIGHT for every human holder of the shipped sets; the census is right; NOT established for a delegated agent whose delegator's leg carries no Layer 1 bound.**
- *Humans.* The pin boots the real `SecurityPlugin` over a real `ObjectQL` and `SqlDriver` with the shipped sets and the baseline composed, twice (declared, and with the key dropped), and compares every persona's served ids on all 23 declarers. The census is right by the code: `resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized` adds `member_default` to every non-agent context with a `userId`; `member_default` carries a literal for each declarer and the `'*'` write floor for `org_member`; for the user in no organisation the floor is outside the positions domain, but each `select`-only default is then filtered out of the write class by `getApplicablePolicies`, and each `all` literal is held, so no human ever collects a default (pinned by identity, `isObjectDefaultRowScopePolicy`). The platform administrator's bypass is decided before the collection (`computeLayeredRlsFilter` skips Layer 1 on `posturePermits && superuserBypass`). Explain for `read` is byte-for-byte for every human. Right.
- *Agents.* An agent's own sets are its ceiling alone (`isAgent` keeps the baseline off), the ceiling carries no row policy (ADR-0090 D10), so the agent leg's collection is empty and now collects each declarer's default on the operations the declaration names, evaluated as the delegator (`userId` is the human). The dev's census of where it is collected (all four operations on the 8 `all` objects, `select` on the other 15) follows from `getApplicablePolicies`. Right. The read door then ANDs the agent leg and the delegator leg (`:4171`–`:4205`). Served rows are unchanged for an agent if and only if the delegator leg already bounds the object at least as tightly as the default. That holds for the pin's member and viewer and, on the better-auth-managed declarers, for its organisation administrator (the admin sets carry an explicit entry without the superuser bits for every object in `BETTER_AUTH_MANAGED_OBJECTS`, so `hasSuperuserReadBypass` is false there and the `_self` literals are collected). It does NOT hold for a PLATFORM ADMINISTRATOR delegator: `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` is one wildcard carrying `viewAllRecords`, with no explicit identity entries; the identity objects declare no `access.default: 'private'` (`getObjectSecurityMeta` reads `isPrivate` from that key alone), so `resolveObjectPermission` returns the wildcard, `posturePermits` holds on the managed objects and on the tenancy-disabled ledger, and the delegator leg's Layer 1 is skipped (null). Before this PR that agent's read carried no row bound on the 23 objects (ceiling leg empty, delegator leg null); after it, the agent leg's default is the only Layer 1 bound, so the platform administrator's agent reads the administrator's own rows where it read every row before, and its `rls` layer moves from no policy to `narrows`. The same follows for any delegator holding an authored policy wider than an object's default. The pin's `mcp agent for the platform admin` persona reports no movement and the same decided explain — but the pin asserts no served set for that persona on either tree (its CONTROLs name the member, the loner, the member's agent and the administrator), so equality there is as consistent with the delegator having resolved to something narrower in the fixture, or with a refusal on both trees, as with the production shape; a read-only record cannot run it, and the pin as written cannot tell. So: the census is right; "no baseline holder's rows move" is right; "an MCP agent acting for a user reads the same rows as before" (the changeset's Unchanged bullet and the PR body) is established only for delegators whose own leg is no wider than the default, and by the code it is false for a platform administrator's agent. Named wrong on that sentence; a condition in ③.
- *Is the explain move inside "byte-for-byte"?* No. For every agent the `rls` prose now names the object default and the composed `readFilter` gains the agent leg's conjunct; the pin relaxes agents to decision-equality, and the PR says so. E′ item 3's "their behaviour and explain output do not move" was written for the holders of the spread policies; the ceiling holder's explain does move. It must be declared, and the changeset's agent bullet declares the prose half; the served-row half is the open point above.
- *The 2026-09-08 depth ruling.* The rule at `explain-engine.ts` about `:805` reads "a ceiling that says nothing subtracts nothing": a delegated principal's silent ceiling contributes NO owner narrowing, every row bound comes from the delegator's leg, and the measurement that produced it was an agent of a `viewAllRecords` user being over-narrowed by its own silent leg. In letter the two rulings do not collide: that one governs access depth, E′ item 2 and the ADR-0095 D1 note govern Layer 1 and say silence means the default. In substance, the agent leg's default is a row bound a silent ceiling now contributes, and it binds exactly when the delegator's leg is wider than the default — the shape the 2026-09-08 ruling refused for depth, and ADR-0090 D10 rule 1's "all row narrowing comes from the delegating user". A vs B by the four axes: real need — a platform administrator's agent (and any wider-authored delegator's) loses rows it had, undeclared, so B has pull that "identical explain text" alone did not; long-term soundness — B keeps the ceiling a pure capability ceiling and leaves E′ item 2 whole for every non-delegated principal, while A makes a ceiling carry Layer 1 by accident of an empty collection; making AI mistakes harder — B is one principal-kind carve-out at the one collection point's delegated call, A is an agent/human asymmetry nobody declared; scope — B is `domain:services`, S, threading the delegated flag to `collectRLSPolicies`' callers. Two rulings meet, so this is the director seat's call, not the dev's and not this record's; B is the lean. The dev's "settled as A here" is not accepted as settled.

**4. The `extend` refusal — RIGHT.** `SchemaRegistry.registerObject` throws `ExtensionDefaultRowScopeRefusedError` when `ownership === 'extend'` and the body's `defaultRowScope !== undefined`, beside the field-type door and before the contributor list is opened (`:3313`), so nothing of a refused contribution lands (pinned: contributors, `defaultRowScope` and the new field all unchanged). `code` is `INVALID_METADATA`, `status` and `httpStatus` 422, `name` set, the message names the object and the package. The fold (`mergeObjectDefinitions`, `:432`) copies only `fields`, `validations`, `indexes`, `label`, `pluralLabel`, `description`, so an accepted key would have been inert; the manifest path (`registerApp`, `:8446`–`:8457`) copies a closed key list off each `objectExtensions` entry and `ObjectExtensionSchema` (`:3974`) is a strict object without the key, so only a programmatic `registerObject(..., 'extend')` reaches the door. Every shipped `extend` still registers: the one `extend` of a platform object is `plugin-auth`'s `authObjectExtensions` on `sys_sso_provider` (fields only, through the manifest path), measured booted; the other two (`showcase_account` in examples, `dc_account` in the downstream-contract fixtures) are not platform objects and carry no key. A contributor setting a default on `sys_user` is refused by name on the booted composition and the declared default stands. "Any `defaultRowScope` on an `extend`" is the right reading of E′ item 4: the ruling's verb is "set or loosen", setting is supplying the key at any value, loosening cannot be told from narrowing for two CEL predicates in general, and the key would be inert on the fold anyway. The unexported class with the shared code follows this package's `#16159` convention (classes stay unexported; consumers compare `code`). Not covered, as before: an ownership `overlay`, which replaces the base body (ADR-0029 D9.2) — carried to #24340's seat in 6259391225, not this card's.

**5. The `sys_audit_log` default and the ADR-0105 D3 strip — RIGHT, closing the carry-over.** `admitCollectedPolicy` runs on the default before `getApplicablePolicies`, and `isPlatformTenantPolicy` keys on `(object, name, using)`; `objectDefaultRowScopePolicy` sets `object` to the declaring object, so the declared `sys_audit_log_org` has the shipped literal's provenance key and is stripped where organisation scoping is off, exactly as the set copy is.
